person.name: Dong Hwi Kim
person.affiliation: Mechanical Engineering & Electrical and Computer Engineering · Seoul National University
person.intro: I am an undergraduate at Seoul National University, double majoring in Mechanical Engineering and Electrical and Computer Engineering. I work at the intersection of robotics, 3D vision, and machine learning.
person.bio: I am an undergraduate researcher in the RPM Robotics Lab with Prof. Ayoung Kim and the AIDAS Lab with Prof. Jaeyoung Do. My current work focuses on 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM and visual data augmentation for robot learning.

research.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM
research.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of camera observations, Gaussian scene representation, and camera trajectory; not an experimental result
research.summary: Investigating 3D Gaussian Splatting for simultaneous localization and mapping. A manuscript is currently in preparation.
research.role: Ongoing research on 3DGS-based SLAM; manuscript in preparation.

sections.heading: Research direction
sections.body: This ongoing project investigates the use of 3D Gaussian Splatting in simultaneous localization and mapping. The goal is to connect camera motion estimation with a 3D representation of the surrounding scene.

sections.heading: Current status
sections.body: The manuscript is in preparation. Further method details, experimental results, and publication information will be shared as the work progresses.

research.title: 3DGS Data Augmentation for Robot Learning
research.image_alt: An FR3 manipulation episode rendered from three camera viewpoints using Gaussian scene assets
research.summary: Developing the 3D Gaussian Splatting augmentation module for a broader robotic dataset effort: reconstructing scenes and rendering manipulation demonstrations from multiple viewpoints.
research.role: Responsible for the 3DGS data augmentation module within a larger collaborative dataset project.

sections.heading: The larger effort
sections.body: This work contributes to an augmented robotic dataset that is being developed toward a publication. My responsibility is the 3D Gaussian Splatting data augmentation module, one component of the larger effort.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.body: The module turns captured workcell imagery and robot demonstrations into reusable 3D scene assets and rendered training views. The current implementation supports FR3 manipulation scenes and multiple calibrated camera viewpoints.

sections.heading: Current status
sections.body: The broader dataset collaboration and its manuscript are in progress. Paper details and additional results will be added as the collaboration progresses.

projects.title: Autonomous Perception for the SNU AI Robot Challenge
projects.image_alt: Team 7's autonomous mecanum-wheel robot in the competition arena
projects.summary: An autonomous mobile robot that identifies, collects, and deposits target objects within a timed arena. I worked on perception and model training.
projects.role: Perception and model training, together with Jinyong Jun.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: A fully autonomous robot had to locate target classes announced at match time, collect the appropriate objects, and deliver them to a storage area. The system had to complete perception, navigation, collection, and delivery without operator input after the start signal.

sections.heading: Our system
sections.body: The team built a mecanum-wheel platform with a Jetson Orin Nano, dual cameras, LiDAR, an IMU, and a passive collector. YOLO instance segmentation supplied visual detections, while navigation and geometric checks supported target selection and collection.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.body: I worked on perception and model training alongside Jinyong Jun. This was one part of the team system, alongside dedicated hardware, drivetrain, navigation, and strategy work.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Team 7 placed second, earning 140 out of 200 points across the two final runs. The competition also provided the opportunity to attend the 2026 World Robot Conference.

projects.title: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
projects.image_alt: Team MRI reconstruction framework using brain and knee experts with Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
projects.summary: Reconstructing brain and knee MRI from undersampled k-space using specialized VarNet models, data augmentation, checkpoint averaging, and ensembling.

sections.heading: The reconstruction problem
sections.body: Accelerating MRI acquisition requires reconstructing images from incomplete frequency-domain measurements. Our team worked with brain and knee data at 4× and 8× acceleration in the 2025 SNU FastMRI Challenge.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: We combined Feature VarNet and FI VarNet with expert models specialized by anatomy and acceleration setting. The training pipeline included MRI-aware augmentation, and the final reconstruction pipeline used checkpoint averaging and ensembling to improve stability.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Team 2rm1000 placed third and received a team prize of KRW 2,500,000. The repository documents training, reconstruction, and evaluation for the submission.

projects.title: Structured Scene Reordering with Multimodal LLMs
projects.image_alt: Diagram of mapping frame-order views into a common coordinate system for Random4 inference
projects.summary: Recovering the chronological order of four shuffled frames from a text description using multimodal reasoning and structured permutation decoding.

sections.heading: The task
sections.body: Given a natural-language storyline and four shuffled images, the model must recover a coherent chronological sequence. This requires reasoning across both visual observations and language, rather than recognizing each image independently.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: The documented submission uses Qwen3.5-27B with LoRA adaptation, structured pairwise and chronological readouts, and a decoder over the 24 possible permutations. Temporal-gap supervision and local hard-negative ranking support training, while Random4 aggregation and late-trajectory weight averaging form the final inference pipeline.

sections.heading: Competition result
sections.body: GeekSeek finished eighth overall in SNU AI Challenge 2026. The linked repository distinguishes the official submission from experiments performed after the competition.

projects.title: Physics-Guided Wind Power Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Zephyr Analytics team cover for the 2025 Wind Power Prediction Competition
projects.summary: A hybrid physics–ML ensemble for hourly wind generation forecasting. I worked on model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.
projects.role: Model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.

sections.heading: The forecasting problem
sections.body: The competition required hourly wind power forecasts for sites in Gyeongju, Yangyang, and Yeongdeok. Forecast quality was evaluated using both prediction error and an economic settlement metric.

sections.heading: A hybrid physics–ML approach
sections.body: Our team used physics-based feature engineering, including air-density estimation informed by the Arden–Buck equation, and a physical power curve as a baseline prediction. A residual LightGBM model corrected remaining errors. The final ensemble combined Ridge Regression, Random Forest, and residual LightGBM, with weights optimized using Optuna.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.body: I worked on model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization. Derrick Junsu Lee led the team and worked on machine learning and testing; Hyunseung Lee worked on preprocessing and feature engineering.

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Zephyr Analytics received third place (Excellence Award) among 270 teams. The reported final metrics were 19.34% NMAE and a 22.09% settlement revenue rate.

projects.title: Automated Filming Device
projects.image_alt: Sunflower-inspired face-tracking camera device with a yellow phone mount and white circular base
projects.summary: A portable hands-free filming device that combines face tracking, motorized pan–tilt motion, and infrared remote control for solo creators.

sections.heading: Motivation
sections.body: Solo creators need to keep a subject framed without continuously adjusting a phone or relying on a camera operator. Our team built a compact filming device that follows a face and can also be repositioned using a remote control.

sections.heading: Hardware
sections.body: The design combines a Raspberry Pi, a wide-view camera, two servo motors for horizontal and vertical motion, an infrared receiver, and a ball-transfer support mechanism. The sunflower-inspired assembly is designed for portability and straightforward assembly.

sections.heading: Software and interaction
sections.body: Visual face tracking drives pan–tilt adjustments. Infrared remote commands provide manual directional control and operating-mode input, while LED indicators communicate device status. The team implementation uses LIRC and NEC infrared commands.

sections.heading: Recognition
sections.body: The project received first prize in the 2024 SNU Mechatronics class and the Grand Prize (first place) in the HD Hyundai Mechatronics Competition, with a team prize of KRW 3,000,000.

projects.title: TaXer & WaXer: Forecasting Periodic Time Series
projects.image_alt: Original presentation slide showing the TaXer periodic feature extraction and cross-attention architecture
projects.summary: Combining explicit periodic feature extraction with transformer forecasting, evaluated on weather and retail time series.

sections.heading: The question
sections.body: Can explicitly extracting periodic features improve transformer-based forecasting on strongly periodic sequences? We explored this question using weather observations and retail sales data.

sections.heading: Two hybrid architectures
sections.body: TaXer incorporates a TimesNet-inspired block that identifies dominant periods and extracts features through 2D temporal modeling. WaXer instead uses WaveNet-inspired dilated causal convolutions. In both variants, the extracted features provide context to the transformer through cross-attention.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.body: The course report compares the hybrids against iTransformer and TimeXer across global weather, Korean weather, and Sticker Sales data. In the reported Sticker Sales comparison, TaXer achieved an MSE of 0.1569 versus 0.1647 for TimeXer.

sections.heading: Team and materials
sections.body: This SNU Introduction to Deep Learning project was completed by Donghwi Kim, Jinwoo Seo, Hyeonseop Shin, and Manyoung Han.
